clue.text: Way to produce order using 26 characters helping a bit as arranged

definitions.text: Way to produce order using 26 characters

indicators.note: the letters are put in a new arrangement

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 13 letters

explanation.surface: Someone explains a filing system that relies on letters doing a small helpful job.
explanation.walkthrough: The 26 characters are the letters of the alphabet; the whole puzzle plays on 13 and its double, 26. 'As' does double duty in the surface but is plain fodder here.
explanation.definitionFit: Alphabetising puts things in order using the 26 letters of the alphabet.

clue.text: Allowing to capture queen – writing on wall, perhaps

indicators.note: one word takes another prisoner inside it

blocks.note: letting = allowing
ER = Elizabeth Regina, placed inside LETT|ING

explanation.surface: A permit to seize a queen, with the message scrawled on a wall like graffiti.
explanation.walkthrough: ER, for Elizabeth Regina, is the crossword's standard queen.
explanation.definitionFit: Lettering is painted or carved writing, such as a sign on a wall.

clue.text: Middle one of 13

blocks.note: the core or centre of something
each card suit holds 13 cards; this is one card of the red suit that is not diamonds

explanation.walkthrough: The heart of a matter is its middle, and a heart is a playing card, one of 13 in its suit; the puzzle keeps returning to that number.
explanation.definitionFit: The heart of a matter is its middle, and a heart is one of the 13 cards in its suit.

clue.text: One of three sea-going tradesmen who understates 13?

definitions.text: One of three sea-going tradesmen who understates 13?

blocks.note: the surface suggests sailors; it means the nursery rhyme 'Rub-a-dub-dub, three men in a tub', whose three tradesmen go to sea
this tradesman's dozen is traditionally 13 loaves, so calling 13 a dozen understates it

explanation.surface: A riddle about a tradesman afloat who plays down a number.
explanation.walkthrough: The butcher, the baker and the candlestick-maker are the three men in the tub. A baker's dozen is 13, so the baker is the one who understates it.
explanation.definitionFit: The baker is one of the three tub-sailors, and his 'dozen' is really 13.

clue.text: Securing 13 at sixes and sevens? Good

indicators.note: in confusion, so the letters are jumbled

blocks.note: the number written out, then jumbled
G = good

explanation.surface: Pinning down a number while everything is in disarray, then a satisfied 'Good'.
explanation.walkthrough: The digits must be spelt out as a word before they can be rearranged; six and seven add up to 13, which makes the indicator a sly fit.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: tethering an animal secures it with a rope or chain.

clue.text: Apparently was moved from hut over a rent

indicators.note: in a down clue, the first part sits above the second

blocks.note: a shed is a hut
a rent is a tear, a rip in cloth

explanation.surface: Something was shifted out of a shed and a hole appeared.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Moved' looks physical, as if something were carried out of the hut; it means emotionally touched. 'Apparently' is fair because a tear is the visible sign of being moved.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who sheds a tear shows outwardly that they were moved.

clue.text: Kind of diet contributing to reduction of a tummy

indicators.note: the answer is part of the words that follow, not the whole

blocks.note: reductioN OF A Tummy

explanation.surface: A diet that helps shrink a belly.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is exactly what such a diet promises, which disguises that the answer is sitting in the text.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: this is one named type of diet, the way low-carb is another.

clue.text: Shout out and sing in a part of US – one of 13 colonies

definitions.text: part of US – one of 13 colonies

indicators.note: 'out' as in inside out: the word's letters are turned out of their usual order

blocks.note: rearranged by 'out'
to carol is to sing
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone yells and sings somewhere in America.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In a' looks like it places the singing inside something, but it simply supplies its own letters. The 13 colonies were the British settlements that became the first US states.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example with a history lesson attached: the state descends from one of the 13 British colonies that declared independence in 1776.

clue.text: Like some Rugby matches I attend here, is mishandled

indicators.note: handled badly, so the letters are knocked out of order

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 13 letters

explanation.surface: A rugby fan admits the matches they go to are badly run.
explanation.walkthrough: Rugby league is played thirteen-a-side, against fifteen in rugby union. 'Mishandled' suits the surface, since a dropped ball is a knock-on.
explanation.definitionFit: Rugby league matches are thirteen-a-side, with 13 players on each team.

clue.text: Both parts of return trip in remote region

blocks.note: the first leg of a round trip, heading away
the second leg, coming home

explanation.surface: A round trip made into the wilds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' reads as setting the trip in the region, but it only links wordplay to definition. The outback is the remote interior of Australia.
explanation.definitionFit: The outback is Australia's remote, thinly populated interior.

clue.text: Some flight flew there, returning before 13th

indicators.note: only a portion of the following words is used
that portion comes back the other way

blocks.note: fligHT FLEW There holds these seven letters; read them backwards

explanation.surface: An aircraft flew somewhere and came back before a certain date.
explanation.walkthrough: The date-like '13th' looks like part of the travel story; it is the definition, since the answer comes just before it in any month.
explanation.definitionFit: The twelfth comes immediately before the thirteenth.

clue.text: Taking one of London’s papers

blocks.note: the definite article, singling out one paper by its title
the Financial Times, a London business daily

explanation.surface: Someone picks up a London newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: The FT is the Financial Times, a London business newspaper, and 'the' goes in front as part of its name. 'Taking' looks like picking up a copy.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: taking, in the sense of stealing, is theft.

clue.text: Person taking part in historical pageants? Not to be confused with career

definitions.text: Person taking part in historical pageants?

indicators.note: things that are confused are muddled together, so the letters lose their order

blocks.note: anagram fodder
anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A pageant performer insists that dressing up is a hobby, not a job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not' reads as a denial, but it is three letters of fodder. This is the puzzle's entry 13; elsewhere '13' mostly means the number itself.
explanation.definitionFit: A re-enactor acts out historical events, often in costumed pageants.

clue.text: French cookery expert, one of 13, possibly

blocks.note: Julia ___, the American TV cook who wrote Mastering the Art of French Cooking
a young person aged thirteen, or one of a family of thirteen offspring

explanation.surface: A famous French chef is counted among 13.
explanation.walkthrough: 'French' suggests a chef from France; Julia Child was American, an expert in French cooking. 'Possibly' covers the loose second sense: a 13-year-old is still a child.
explanation.definitionFit: Julia Child was the celebrated expert on French cookery, and a child may be aged 13.

clue.text: Setter, for example, including double anagram for old weapon

indicators.note: one part holds another inside it
names the operation outright: DOUBLE is rearranged

blocks.note: a setter is a breed of dog; opened as DO|G
DOUBLE rearranged, placed inside DOG

explanation.surface: A crossword setter uses a twin anagram to clue an old weapon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Setter' looks like the compiler of the puzzle; it is a dog. 'Double anagram' sounds like jargon, but 'anagram' is the instruction to rearrange 'double'. A doodlebug was the V-1 flying bomb of the Second World War.
explanation.definitionFit: Doodlebug was the British nickname for the German V-1 flying bomb of 1944.

clue.text: Line written in regret after another splits party – that can speed up division

indicators.note: the line is put inside the word for regret
this part follows the other in the answer
the second L breaks the party word apart

blocks.note: a side is a party in a dispute
another line, placed inside S|IDE
to rue is to regret
L = line, placed inside RU|E

explanation.surface: A sorry note sent after a quarrel divides a group, with a hint of speeding up a split.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Division' looks like the split in the party; it is arithmetic. Before calculators, a slide rule did multiplication and division quickly.
explanation.definitionFit: A slide rule is a sliding ruler used to multiply and divide quickly.

clue.text: Farm worker has drink in piece of pottery

indicators.note: the worker is built around the drink
the drink goes inside the pottery word

blocks.note: sherd = shard, a broken piece of pottery; opened as S|HERD
placed inside SHERD

explanation.surface: A farmhand keeps a drink in a bit of broken crockery.
explanation.walkthrough: SHERD is the archaeologist's spelling of shard.
explanation.definitionFit: A swineherd is a farm worker who tends pigs.

clue.text: Less than 13 given to bidder? That’s dishonest

blocks.note: under = less than
in bridge each player, who bids, is dealt a hand of 13 cards

explanation.surface: Someone at an auction is short-changed, and calls it a swindle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bidder' suggests an auction; it is a bridge player, who bids after being dealt 13 cards.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: underhand behaviour is sly and dishonest, done out of sight.

clue.text: For instance, din in arena is on the rise again

indicators.note: the first parts go inside the arena word

blocks.note: a boxing ring is an arena; opened as R|ING
e.g. = for instance
a row (rhymes with cow) is a racket

explanation.surface: The noise in a stadium is getting louder once more.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface makes 'on the rise' the noise building; it means growing again. ROW here is a loud noise, not a line.
explanation.definitionFit: Something regrowing is rising up again after being cut back.

clue.text: Frenchman who sculpted river-god

blocks.note: R = river, as on maps
Odin, chief of the Norse gods

explanation.surface: A French sculptor carved a statue of a river-god.
explanation.walkthrough: The hyphen in 'river-god' fuses what the wordplay treats as two separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Auguste Rodin was the French sculptor of The Thinker.

clue.text: I strolled haphazardly, like most aristocratic types

indicators.note: without order, so the letters are scrambled

blocks.note: anagram fodder

explanation.surface: Someone wandered aimlessly, as idle nobles do.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strolled' reads as the aristocrats' leisurely walk, but its letters are fodder along with 'I'.
explanation.definitionFit: Lordliest means most like a lord, the grandest of aristocrats.

clue.text: One of 26 on radio, partnered with one of 13

blocks.note: the NATO radio code word for R, one of the 26 letters
Shakespeare's Juliet is 13, and this is the lover she is partnered with

explanation.walkthrough: The NATO radio alphabet gives each of the 26 letters a word: Alpha, Bravo, ... Romeo. Shakespeare's Juliet is not yet 14.
explanation.definitionFit: Romeo is the radio word for R, and Romeo was partnered with the 13-year-old Juliet.

clue.text: Land part of Peter Rabbit

indicators.note: only a section of the following words is used

blocks.note: peTER RAbbit

explanation.surface: Peter Rabbit, Beatrix Potter's character, owns some land.
explanation.walkthrough: Peter Rabbit is Beatrix Potter's rabbit; the name is just the carrier, with the Latin word for land spanning its two words.
explanation.definitionFit: Terra is Latin for land, used in English as in terra firma.

clue.text: Cause for complaint from man in Latin America

blocks.note: vir is Latin for man
US = United States

explanation.surface: A grievance comes from a man in South or Central America.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Latin America' reads as one place; split it into 'in Latin' and 'America'. A complaint here is an illness, not a grumble.
explanation.definitionFit: A virus causes a complaint in the medical sense, an ailment.

clue.text: Record second half for South American city

indicators.note: keep only the back half of the word

blocks.note: capital of Uruguay, ten letters; keep the last five

explanation.surface: A record of a second half of a match, filmed in a South American city.
explanation.walkthrough: Montevideo, capital of Uruguay, has ten letters, so its second five are the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, as verbs: to video an event is to record it on camera.

clue.text: Mediterranean islander backed as OK for nomination

indicators.note: the letters are read back to front

blocks.note: a man from Elba, the island of Napoleon's first exile; read it backwards

explanation.surface: A man from a Mediterranean island is endorsed as a suitable candidate.
explanation.walkthrough: Elba is the Mediterranean island where Napoleon was exiled, a crossword favourite.
explanation.definitionFit: Something namable can be named, so it is fit for nomination.

clue.text: Punishment for player, one of 26

blocks.note: what a football referee shows to send a player off
a pack has 52 cards, and the 26 hearts and diamonds share one colour

explanation.walkthrough: A pack holds two red suits of 13 cards each, making 26 red cards.
explanation.definitionFit: A red card sends a player off, and each heart or diamond is a red card.

clue.text: Trump listened to group of 13 unsophisticated types

indicators.note: the word is heard, not seen, so its sound is what counts

blocks.note: to ruff is to play a trump in cards
the diamond suit has 13 cards

explanation.surface: A politician heeds a gang of simple people.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital T makes 'Trump' look like the politician; it is the card-game verb. A rough diamond is a good-hearted person with coarse manners.
explanation.definitionFit: Rough diamonds are kind-hearted people lacking polish or refinement.
